name: The Headless Horseman
franchise: "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" story by Washington Irving
pitch: The story of the Headless Horseman and the character itself really embody Halloween. Spooky horseman with a pumpkin for a head? In New England? Come on now...

moves.name: Pumpkin Catapult
moves.description: Launches a flaming jack-o’-lantern across the arena. A seasonal projectile with absolutely no return policy.

moves.name: Midnight Gallop
moves.description: Charges through the fog on a spectral horse, knocking opponents off balance before vanishing into the trees.

name: Hannibal Lecter
franchise: Silence of the Lambs, Red Dragon, Manhunter films and books.
pitch: Super creepy, and played brilliantly by the likes of Anthony Hopkins, Brian Cox, and Mads Mikkelsen. Lecter gets inside the audience’s head, and really defines a Halloween horror experience.

moves.name: Dinner Invitation
moves.description: Sets an impeccably polite trap. The opponent loses their guard while trying to remember which fork to use.

moves.name: Mind Palace
moves.description: Reads the opponent’s next move and answers with a perfectly timed psychological counterattack.

name: The Shapeshifter from "The Thing"
pitch: It can become anyone with near-perfect accuracy. Nothing scarier than waking up next to an exact copy of yourself. Are you sure you're the real one? Even if you are, who will believe you?

moves.name: Perfect Copy
moves.description: Mimics the opponent’s appearance and fighting stance, turning every teammate into a potential suspect.

moves.name: Biomass Breakout
moves.description: Unfolds into an impossible tangle of limbs. A close-range surprise with very poor personal boundaries.

name: The Jeans from the movie Slaxx
pitch: A pair of jeans possessed by the spirit of a child worker who died picking the cotton they're made from. It strangles its victims. You'll never want to wear unethically sourced denim again! 👖

moves.name: Denim Death Grip
moves.description: Wraps both trouser legs around the target and squeezes. Somehow still advertised as a relaxed fit.

moves.name: Runway Rampage
moves.description: Skates across the shop floor in a spinning denim rush. Fast fashion gets a very literal combo attack.

name: Michael Myers
pitch: The mask. The music. The fact that he never runs and still catches everyone. Michael Myers makes a quiet suburban street terrifying, and Halloween is literally his franchise. Give the man his crown.

moves.name: Suburban Stalk
moves.description: Advances at walking speed yet somehow closes every gap. Sprinting opponents waste stamina in disbelief.

moves.name: Final Frame
moves.description: Absorbs a finishing blow, disappears from view, and returns when the opponent looks away.

name: Ursula
pitch: Ursula turns every scene into a spectacle: sharp, funny, ambitious, and backed by one of Disney’s best villain songs. She makes a dangerous deal feel irresistible, then nearly wins. That blend of theatrical flair and real menace earns her the crown.

moves.name: Fine Print
moves.description: Offers a tempting power-up with a disastrous hidden clause. The opponent’s strongest ability becomes collateral.

moves.name: Tidal Tantrum
moves.description: Whips up a towering whirlpool and sends the entire arena spinning to her dramatic finale.

name: Chucky
pitch:
Dolls are possessed and alive y'all. Stay awake with one eye open (they watch while you sleep). 

Fun fact, if your babysitter lets you watch Child's Play at 6 years old, you will insist on throwing away every toy doll you were given (only LEGO bricks are safe), and you will have a lifelong fear of dolls.

moves.name: Toybox Ambush
moves.description: Plays lifeless until the opponent steps close, then springs out with a tiny but thoroughly unpleasant combo.

moves.name: Batteries Not Included
moves.description: Shrugs off a seemingly decisive hit and comes back talking trash. The warranty does not cover this.

name: Beetlejuice
pitch: Overall kookiness + proximity to Catherine O'Hara

moves.name: Say It Thrice
moves.description: Builds power with each repetition of his name, then bursts into the arena with a wildly excessive entrance.

moves.name: Bio-Exorcism
moves.description: Rearranges the scenery into a ridiculous haunted obstacle course. Gravity is invited but not consulted.

name: The Mothman
pitch: Scariest cryptid of all time

moves.name: Red-Eye Warning
moves.description: Fixes the opponent with an ominous stare, rattling their timing with the feeling that something is about to happen.

moves.name: Bridge-Side Glide
moves.description: Sweeps overhead in a silent aerial pass, leaving a disorienting gust and several unanswered questions.

name: The Beast
pitch: from the wiki: "He uses psychological manipulation, umbrakinesis (darkness control), and haunting opera singing"

moves.name: Lantern Bargain
moves.description: Offers a way out of the darkness, then turns the promise into another reason to keep wandering.

moves.name: Blackwood Aria
moves.description: Sends a haunting note through the trees. Shadows close in while the opponent struggles to find the path.

name: Mel and Charlie Jones (Coraline's Parents)
pitch: The Beldam is just doing what monsters do. The real villains are Coraline's parents. Their constant emotional neglect and refusal to pay attention to their daughter created the exact vulnerability the monster needed to trap her. They are the true catalysts for the horror.

moves.name: Not Now, Coraline
moves.description: Deflects an incoming plea with a distracted wave. The opponent’s dramatic monologue fails to connect.

moves.name: Deadline Double-Team
moves.description: Both parents bury themselves in work, creating an impenetrable wall of keyboards and unfinished conversations.

name: Seymour Krelborn
pitch: Audrey II gets the credit as the monster, but Seymour is the enabler. To get fame, wealth, and the girl, he actively chooses to chop up bodies and feed humans to an alien plant instead of just going back to being an ordinary florist. He is the true villain.

moves.name: Feed Me Combo
moves.description: Calls in a very hungry plant assist. What began as a small gardening problem becomes everyone’s problem.

moves.name: Suddenly, Cover-Up
moves.description: Distracts the opponent with an innocent florist routine while sweeping the latest terrible decision out of sight.

name: Pennywise the Clown
pitch: Made us see Ronald McDonald in a whole new light

moves.name: Fear Buffet
moves.description: Transforms into a theatrical version of the opponent’s worst fear, scaling the scare to their imagination.

moves.name: Storm-Drain Surprise
moves.description: Baits the opponent with a bright balloon, then reappears from an unexpected corner of the arena.

name: Freddy Krueger
pitch: He stalks and kills you in your dreams. The perfect formula for years of nightmares.

moves.name: Dream Rewrite
moves.description: Turns the arena into a nightmare tailored to the opponent. The floor plan is no longer accepting complaints.

moves.name: Bedtime Slash
moves.description: Waits for the opponent’s concentration to slip, then strikes with a razor-gloved dream combo.

name: Jason Voorhees
pitch: 12 films. That's a lot of murders.

moves.name: Campground Cleave
moves.description: Delivers a heavy, deliberate strike that makes flimsy cover feel like a very optimistic choice.

moves.name: Lake Return
moves.description: Drops out of sight and rises again from the water. The opponent discovers the fight was only on intermission.

name: The Babadook
pitch: Terrifying basement-dwelling monster or haunting allegory about grief and trauma? You decide (note: I cannot watch scary movies so everything I know about this film comes from Wikipedia and Instagram reels)

moves.name: Pop-Up Panic
moves.description: Unfolds from a storybook silhouette and stretches across the arena, turning a quiet page into a jump scare.

moves.name: Basement Encore
moves.description: Retreats into the dark and returns with renewed pressure. Ignoring the problem only adds another verse.

name: Vecna
pitch: A classic human-turned-monster origin story, an army of Demogorgons, and the power to make me scared of every flickering light in my apartment :)

moves.name: Grandfather Chime
moves.description: Marks the opponent with an ominous clock cue, counting down to a powerful psychic strike.

moves.name: Upside-Down Crush
moves.description: Lifts the target with telekinetic force while vines take control of the battlefield.

name: Nikki Freeman
pitch: She brings the kind of horror that feels a little too real and makes you uncomfortable in the worst way possible…and don’t even get me started on that horrifying smile 😭

moves.name: Unbroken Smile
moves.description: Holds an unnerving smile just a little too long, disrupting the opponent’s focus before they can commit to an attack.

moves.name: Too Close
moves.description: Closes the distance with relentless attention. Every attempted retreat becomes another uncomfortable encounter.

name: A Murder (otherwise known as a flock of crows)
pitch: Crows and ravens have always been associated with Halloween, horror, and lore as symbols of death and dark omens. Also used as an ominous creature by E.A. Poe

moves.name: Murder Formation
moves.description: The flock dives in coordinated waves, turning one easy-to-dodge bird into a screen full of trouble.

moves.name: Playground Omen
moves.description: Quietly gathers behind the opponent until the arena is crowded with beaks, wings, and very bad possibilities.

name: Annabelle
pitch: A porcelain doll, based on a real Raggedy Ann doll, deemed possessed; moved itself and objects; supposedly attacked a person and left scratches: investigated and ultimately kept locked in the basement of paranormal investigators, the Warrens.  It now resides in their haunted museum, in Salem, MA.

moves.name: Shelf Shift
moves.description: Moves only when nobody is watching, making distance and locked doors feel suspiciously unreliable.

moves.name: Porcelain Proxy
moves.description: Sits perfectly still while a sinister presence does the attacking. Excellent energy efficiency; terrible houseguest.

name: Thing
pitch: It's a hand above the rest! Give it a hand. You gotta hand it to ’em! Hand me that hat! Hand it over, I said! I could do this all day, but I have to go hand out candy.

moves.name: Five-Finger Feint
moves.description: Distracts with a friendly wave, then slips past the opponent’s guard with astonishing fingerwork.

moves.name: The Helping Hand
moves.description: Vaults across the arena to intercept an attack. A loyal assist move with a surprisingly firm grip.
